cues.en: You can you can separate your state into different kinds of things, um, and you can have methods that only work on the those pieces of state and we call those objects.

cues.en: Other than to just say that, you know, functional programming does have a completely different set of answers to a similar problem.

cues.zh: 所以在面向对象编程里，他们说，让我们组织状态，用对象，把程序看作相互作用的代理。

cues.zh: 函数式编程则同意状态令人困惑，但主张：让我们避开它。
cues.en: Functional programming, instead agrees state is confusing, but says, let's avoid it.

cues.zh: 干脆说状态是不好的。

cues.zh: 我说状态，指的是任何原地改变的值。
cues.en: And when I say state, I mean any values that change in place.

cues.en: So if you have an array and you want to increment it in an imperative programming language, you just increment that array.

cues.zh: 在函数式编程里，我们会说：不行，这很糟糕。
cues.en: And in functional programming, we'd say, you know what, no, that's bad.

cues.zh: 因为这样当这些数组被传给某个函数，而那个函数修改了它，我们却没料到，就会出问题。
cues.en: Because then when these arrays being passed to some function and that function changes it, and we didn't expect that, things go wrong.

cues.zh: 基本上，状态就是万恶之源。
cues.en: Like basically state is the root of all problems.

cues.zh: 所以我们尽量避开它。
cues.en: So let's try to avoid it.

cues.zh: 那么，和经典的命令式编程相比，函数式编程语言还给了我们一个新工具，那就是函数。
cues.en: Now, compared to, you know, classical imperative programming and functional programming functional programming languages also gave us a new tool, and that was the function.

cues.zh: 这是为了区分——我们用“函数”这个词，正是为了区别于“过程”这个概念。
cues.en: And that's to distinguish and we use the word function to really distinguish from the idea of a procedure.

cues.zh: 函数和过程的主要区别在于：过程嘛，你得声明它、必须给它一个名字，而且你仍然可以传递过程，也许是按名字传递。
cues.en: And the the main difference between a function and a procedure is that a procedure, you know, you can declare, you have to give it a name, and you can still pass procedures around, maybe by name.

cues.zh: 可以把过程的名字传来传去。
cues.en: You can pass the names of procedures around.

cues.zh: 但你不能把一个动态创建的函数当作值传出去，而函数就可以。
cues.en: But you can't uh pass a given function that you create dynamically as a value, whereas with functions, you can.

cues.zh: 所以过程没法按值传递，也没法随手创建再传出去，而函数可以。
cues.en: So procedures can't really be passed around by value and you can't create them on the fly and pass them around, whereas with functions you can.

cues.zh: 如果你用过 JavaScript，就知道匿名函数到处都是，所以这个概念也没那么离谱。
cues.en: Now if you work with JavaScript, you know, anonymous functions, um, you know, they're they're everywhere and so you it's it's not that crazy of a concept.

cues.zh: 但在当时，这绝对是很不一样的东西；如果你用的是严格的面向对象语言，它们并没有这种可以随便传递的函数。
cues.en: Um, but at the time it was definitely something very different and if you work in like a strict object-oriented programming language, they don't really have um they don't have these functions that you can just pass around.

cues.zh: 有时它们也被叫作 Lambda。
cues.en: Sometimes they're they're also called Lambdas.

cues.zh: 嗯，但他们没有这个，比如 Java 直到最近才让函数可以单独传递。
cues.en: Um, but they don't have them, like Java only recently, you know, had made it possible to pass around functions on their own.

cues.zh: 呃，而且几乎没人用，因为，你知道，为什么需要函数？对象上有方法就够了。
cues.en: Uh, and barely anyone uses that, because, you know, why do you need functions? You just have methods on objects.

cues.zh: 但在函数式编程里，我们说，不不，我们不需要对象，只要有个函数就行。
cues.en: But in functional programming, we say, no, no, we don't need an object, you can just have a function.

cues.zh: 它可以独立存在。
cues.en: It can just sit on its own.

cues.zh: 而函数式编程的模型，这种心智模型，不是达成某个解决方案的步骤，也不是相互交互的代理。
cues.en: And the the model, the mental model of functional programming isn't steps to achieve some solution, isn't interacting agents working with each other.

cues.zh: 它主要就是把程序看作从输入到输出的管道。
cues.en: It's really mostly thinking of a program as a pipeline of input to output.

cues.zh: 我们会想，好，我们的程序将要接收的数据是什么？
cues.en: We think of, okay, what is the data that our program is going to be receiving?

cues.zh: 随着时间推移，以及我们如何把这些数据转换成想要的输出。
cues.en: Over time, and how do we transform that data into the outputs that we want.

cues.zh: 现在你可能会想，我们想避免状态，但可变状态和副作用是不可避免的。
cues.en: Now, you might be thinking, well, we want to avoid state, but mutable state and side effects are inescapable.

cues.zh: 这几乎正是编程的意义所在。
cues.en: That's kind of almost the point of programming.

cues.zh: 我们希望程序能做点事，产生一些副作用。
cues.en: We want our programs to do something, have some side effect.

cues.zh: 如果我们的程序只是让笔记本更热，然后为宇宙的热寂添一份热，那它其实没什么用。
cues.en: If all our program did was just make our laptop hotter and then contribute to the heat of death of the universe, it wouldn't really be useful.

cues.zh: 我是说，除非你觉得冷。
cues.en: I mean, unless you're cold.

cues.zh: 呃，但你知道，程序的目的就是做点事，哪怕至少只是打印出一个数字。
cues.en: Um, but, you know, the purpose of programs is to do something, even if at the least, it's to print out a single number.

cues.zh: 如果我们只想接收一堆输入并打印出一个数字，那仍然是副作用——它在向控制台打印。
cues.en: If all we want to do is take in a bunch of inputs and print out a number, that's still some side effect. It's printing to the console.

cues.zh: 呃，但你知道，通常真实程序还有我们会考虑的其他副作用。
cues.en: Um, but, you know, there's typically, you know, real programs have other side effects that we think about.

cues.zh: 比如，嗯，跟数据库通信、修改数据库里的内容、发邮件、触发其他外部 API、向另一台服务器发 HTTP 请求，嗯，或者写入文件系统。
cues.en: And it's things like, you know, um, communicating to a database and changing things in a database, sending an email or triggering some other external API, making an HTTP request to another server, um, or writing to the file system.

cues.zh: 这些大致都是程序通常会对计算机系统其他部分产生的那类影响。
cues.en: These are all kind of effects that a program typically what we would want a program to have on other parts of your computer system.

cues.zh: 所以函数式编程会说，好吧，是的，我们确实需要副作用。
cues.en: So functional programming would say, okay, yes, we do want side effects.

cues.zh: 所以它并不是说要把所有状态都去掉，把所有副作用都去掉。
cues.en: And so it's not saying let's get rid of all state, let's get rid of all kind of side effects.

cues.zh: 函数式编程是说，但我们要尽力避免它。
cues.en: Functional programming is saying, but let's just do our best to avoid it.

cues.en: How do we avoid actually mutating that state in our programs, and how do we avoid all these other kinds of side effects?

cues.en: But if we make this one no longer mutate the array, we have to move that mutation somewhere else.

cues.en: Like, ideally we would have a bunch of pure functions.

cues.en: We kind of have three functional programming has like three techniques.

cues.en: And those are minimizing, concentrating and deferring.

cues.en: So minimizing is just trying to have less, less state, so less values that we're keeping around.

cues.en: So you know, we're just moving things, we're not decreasing at all, but we're concentrating a little bit.
